experiences.name: Tulum Ruins & Beach Combo Day Trip

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cancun
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Playa Delfines Beach Day
experiences.description: Spend a relaxing day at one of Cancun's most beautiful and uncrowded public beaches. Playa Delfines offers stunning turquoise waters, soft white sand, and the iconic Cancun sign for photos. No entry fee and great waves for bodyboarding.
experiences.location: Hotel Zone (Zona Hotelera), southern end, Cancun

experiences.name: Mercado 28 Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in local Yucatecan cuisine at Cancun's beloved Mercado 28. Sample cochinita pibil tacos, marquesitas (crispy crepes), fresh ceviche, and aguas frescas. Interact with local vendors and experience authentic Mexican food culture away from the tourist strip.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Cancun International Airport at 11:00 AM on Flight AA. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange budget-friendly airport transfer (ADO bus ~$10 USD) to Cancun Beach Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with the hotel and surrounding area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short walk or cheap local bus (R-1 route, ~$0.50 USD) to the nearby Hotel Zone beach access. Spend the afternoon relaxing on the beach, getting your first taste of the turquoise Caribbean waters. Explore the immediate surroundings of the resort and locate nearby amenities.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Hotel Zone boulevard at sunset. Grab dinner at a casual, affordable local eatery near the resort. Head back to the hotel early to rest after travel.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport or grab a snack on the plane before arrival
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick and cheap meal from a local taqueria or convenience store near the hotel (~$4-6 USD)
meals.dinner: El Fish Fritanga or a nearby local seafood stand in the Hotel Zone for affordable fish tacos and grilled seafood (~$8-12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities begin only after 11:00 AM arrival. Keep energy light as travel fatigue may set in. Exchange some currency or withdraw pesos from an ATM at the airport for better rates. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a budget breakfast at the hotel or a nearby local café. Head to Playa Delfines Beach for a full morning session — one of Cancun's most iconic and uncrowded public beaches with stunning views of the Hotel Zone. Arrive early to claim a good spot. Entry is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying Playa Delfines or walk along the shoreline. Bring snacks and water from a nearby OXXO convenience store to save on costs. Explore the beach's natural surroundings and take in the panoramic views of the Caribbean Sea.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to freshen up, then head to Mercado 28 for a street food dinner. Sample local Yucatecan dishes like cochinita pibil tacos, salbutes, and fresh agua fresca at very affordable prices.

meals.breakfast: Pan dulce and café de olla from a local panadería near the hotel (~$2-3 USD)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks from OXXO (chips, fruit, drinks) to enjoy at Playa Delfines (~$3-5 USD)
meals.dinner: Mercado 28 street food stalls — cochinita pibil tacos, salbutes, and fresh juice (~$6-10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Playa Delfines is accessible via the R-1 public bus (~$0.50 USD each way). Bring sunscreen, a hat, and reef-safe sunblock. No beach chairs or umbrellas are provided, so bring a towel or mat. Mercado 28 is best visited in the evening when it's lively.

day_by_day.morning: Take the public bus to Playa Tortugas or Playa Langosta — two more beautiful and accessible public beaches in the Hotel Zone. Enjoy morning swimming in calmer waters, ideal for snorkeling if you bring your own gear. Arrive early to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Hotel Zone's free public beach paths and explore different beach spots. Stop at a local beach shack for a cold coconut water or fresh fruit. Visit the free lookout point near Playa Delfines for panoramic photos of the coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Head into Downtown Cancun (El Centro) via local bus for a more authentic and affordable evening. Browse local shops and explore Parque Las Palapas, a free public square with street performers and local vendors.

meals.breakfast: Huevos rancheros or chilaquiles at a local comedor in El Centro (~$3-5 USD)
meals.lunch: Fresh ceviche or grilled fish at a beachside palapa shack (~$6-8 USD)
meals.dinner: Tacos and tortas at Parque Las Palapas street food vendors (~$4-7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Public beaches in the Hotel Zone are free to access. The R-1 and R-2 bus routes connect most areas for under $1 USD. Downtown Cancun (El Centro) is much more affordable than the Hotel Zone for food and shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Join the Mercado 28 Street Food Tour in the morning to immerse yourself in local Yucatecan cuisine. Sample cochinita pibil tacos, marquesitas, tamales, and fresh tropical fruits. Learn about the culture and culinary traditions of the Yucatan Peninsula from local vendors.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the food tour, explore Mercado 23, a smaller and more local market nearby, for fresh produce, spices, and handmade crafts at very low prices. Pick up affordable souvenirs like hand-painted pottery or woven goods.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the beach for a golden hour swim and sunset viewing at Playa Delfines or the nearest Hotel Zone beach access. End the evening with a relaxed dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Included or sampled as part of the Mercado 28 Street Food Tour
meals.lunch: Continue sampling at Mercado 28 or grab a comida corrida (set lunch menu) at a local restaurant (~$5-7 USD)
meals.dinner: Budget seafood at a local marisquería near the hotel — shrimp cocktail, fish tacos (~$8-12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The Mercado 28 Street Food Tour is a highlight for budget travelers as it offers maximum flavor for minimal cost. Bring small bills (pesos) for market vendors. Mercado 23 is a great place to stock up on snacks and fresh fruit for beach days.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Isla Mujeres via public ferry from Puerto Juárez (round trip ~$10-15 USD). Arrive early and rent a golf cart or bicycle to explore the island. Visit Playa Norte, consistently rated one of the best beaches in the Caribbean, with crystal-clear shallow waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon snorkeling at MUSA (Museo Subacuático de Arte) reef area or simply relax on Playa Norte's white sands. Explore the colorful streets of Isla Mujeres town and browse artisan shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun via ferry before sunset. Freshen up at the hotel and enjoy a leisurely dinner at a beachfront spot or local restaurant near Cancun Beach Resort.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café before heading to the ferry (~$3-5 USD)
meals.lunch: Fresh ceviche, fish tacos, or grilled lobster (in season) at an affordable local restaurant on Isla Mujeres (~$8-12 USD)
meals.dinner: Casual dinner near the hotel — grilled chicken or fish plate at a local comedor (~$7-10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Ferries to Isla Mujeres depart from Puerto Juárez (not the Hotel Zone ferry, which is more expensive). Take the R-1 bus to Puerto Juárez to save money. Bring cash, sunscreen, and a reusable water bottle. The island is very walkable but a rented bicycle ($10/day) makes it more fun.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Cancun — head to your favorite beach one last time for a farewell swim. Playa Delfines is ideal for a peaceful, uncrowded morning session. Take final photos and soak in the Caribbean views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel to pack up and check out. Store luggage at the hotel if your flight is later. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at Mercado 28 or local shops in El Centro for the best prices.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport via ADO bus (~$10 USD) with plenty of time before departure. Enjoy a final budget meal at the airport or a nearby taqueria before flying home.

meals.breakfast: Final Mexican breakfast — chilaquiles or tamales at a local café near the hotel (~$4-6 USD)
meals.lunch: Light lunch or snack at Mercado 28 or a street food stand before heading to the airport (~$4-6 USD)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or a final taco stop near the airport (~$6-10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed. The ADO bus from the Hotel Zone to the airport is the most budget-friendly transfer option. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5-3 hours before international departure. Keep some pesos for tips and last-minute purchases.

trip_options.title: Classic Cancun Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Mercado 28 Street Food Tour

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Cancun International Airport at 11:00 AM on Flight AA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange ground transportation to Cancun Beach Resort. Check-in and settle into your room (early check-in subject to availability). Freshen up and orient yourself with the resort amenities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head down to the resort beach or the nearby Hotel Zone beach for a relaxed first afternoon. Take a leisurely swim, soak up the Caribbean sun, and decompress from travel. Walk along the shoreline to get a feel for the area and spot nearby landmarks.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Blvd Kukulcan in the Hotel Zone for a casual first evening. Explore the shops and enjoy the vibrant atmosphere before settling in for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick bite at the airport before or after landing — try a torta or fresh fruit from an airport café.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the resort restaurant or a nearby casual spot like La Fisheria for fresh seafood tacos and agua fresca.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Labná Restaurant (Hotel Zone) — a mid-range Mexican restaurant known for authentic Yucatecan dishes like sopa de lima and poc chuc. Budget ~$20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Since arrival is at 11:00 AM, keep Day 1 light and relaxed. Confirm check-in time with Cancun Beach Resort in advance to avoid waiting with luggage. Exchange some currency or use an ATM at the airport for local pesos.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a full morning at Playa Delfines Beach Day. Head to one of Cancun's most scenic and uncrowded public beaches, famous for its panoramic views of the turquoise Caribbean and the iconic Cancun sign. Arrive early (around 9:00 AM) to claim a good spot. Swim, relax, and enjoy the natural beauty without the heavy resort crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Hotel Zone and spend the afternoon exploring Mercado Coral Negro (a local flea and artisan market nearby) or relax by the resort pool. Consider renting a kayak or paddleboard from a beach vendor near the Hotel Zone for some light water activity.
day_by_day.evening: Head out for a sunset walk along the Hotel Zone lagoon side for golden-hour views, then dinner at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort or a nearby café like 100% Natural — known for fresh juices, fruit bowls, and healthy Mexican breakfast options. Budget ~$10–15.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and drinks for the beach, or grab street tacos from a vendor near Playa Delfines. Budget ~$5–8.
meals.dinner: Dinner at El Fish Fritanga — a beloved local seafood spot in the Hotel Zone with great grilled fish and shrimp at reasonable prices. Budget ~$15–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Playa Delfines is a public beach with no entrance fee and limited shade — bring sunscreen, a beach umbrella if possible, and plenty of water. Taxis or the R-1 public bus along Blvd Kukulcan are affordable ways to get there.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day experience: Isla Mujeres Snorkeling & Beach Tour. Depart early (around 8:00–9:00 AM) from Puerto Juárez ferry terminal (a short taxi ride from the Hotel Zone). Take the 20-minute ferry to Isla Mujeres. Join a guided snorkeling tour to explore vibrant coral reefs and marine life in the crystal-clear Caribbean waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: After snorkeling, spend the afternoon on Playa Norte — consistently rated one of the best beaches in Mexico. Relax on the calm, shallow turquoise waters. Rent a golf cart (~$40–50 for a few hours) to explore the charming island village, colorful streets, and scenic cliffs at the southern tip.
day_by_day.evening: Return via ferry to Cancun by early evening (last ferries run around 8:00–9:00 PM). Wind down with a relaxed dinner back in the Hotel Zone.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — keep it light (yogurt, fruit, toast).
meals.lunch: Lunch on Isla Mujeres at Olivia Restaurant or a beachside palapa restaurant on Playa Norte. Try fresh ceviche, grilled lobster, or fish tacos. Budget ~$15–25 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Roots Bar & Grill in the Hotel Zone — a chill mid-range spot with Caribbean-inspired dishes and live music some evenings. Budget ~$20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Snorkeling tours from Isla Mujeres typically cost $30–60 per person and include equipment. Book in advance or at the ferry dock. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, as it is required in protected marine areas. Ferry tickets are approximately $10–12 round trip.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day trip: Tulum Ruins & Beach Combo Day Trip. Depart by 7:30–8:00 AM (arrange a shared shuttle or tour from your hotel, ~$40–60 per person round trip). Arrive at the Tulum Archaeological Zone mid-morning. Explore the stunning Mayan ruins perched dramatically on seaside cliffs overlooking the Caribbean — one of the most photogenic sites in Mexico.
day_by_day.afternoon: After touring the ruins, descend to the beach below the cliffs for a swim in the turquoise waters. Spend the afternoon relaxing on the beach or exploring the nearby Tulum town for artisan shops and local color.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun by early evening (approximately 2–2.5 hour drive). Rest briefly at the resort before heading out for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — eggs, fruit, and coffee to fuel the day.
meals.lunch: Lunch near the Tulum ruins at a local restaurant in Tulum town, such as El Camello Jr. for fresh seafood or La Nave for wood-fired pizza. Budget ~$12–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mercado 28 area or a Hotel Zone restaurant like La Parrilla — a lively Mexican grill with great fajitas, guacamole, and margaritas. Budget ~$20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Tulum ruins entrance fee is approximately $5–10 USD. Wear comfortable walking shoes, as the site involves uneven terrain. The beach at Tulum is public but some access points near beach clubs may charge a fee. Bring cash for entrance fees and small vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day adventure: Cenote Dos Ojos Swimming & Snorkeling. Depart by 8:00 AM via shared shuttle or tour (located near Tulum, ~2 hours from Cancun). Explore the magical underground cenote system of Dos Ojos — one of the world's longest underwater cave systems. Snorkel or swim through crystal-clear freshwater passages illuminated by shafts of natural light filtering through the jungle canopy above.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cenote experience, visit a second cenote in the area if time allows (Gran Cenote is nearby and equally stunning). Return to Cancun in the mid-to-late afternoon. Stop at a local roadside stand for fresh coconut water or snacks on the way back.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the final full evening enjoying the Hotel Zone. Take a sunset stroll, browse souvenir shops, or enjoy a beachside cocktail at the resort before a special farewell dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before early departure.
meals.lunch: Pack a light lunch or snacks for the cenote visit, as food options near Dos Ojos are limited. Alternatively, stop at a roadside comedor (local diner) for a hearty set menu lunch (~$8–12).
meals.dinner: Celebratory farewell dinner at Harry's Prime Steakhouse & Raw Bar — a mid-to-upscale restaurant in the Hotel Zone with excellent steaks, seafood, and Caribbean views. Budget ~$35–55 per person for a special treat.

day_by_day.notes: Cenote Dos Ojos entrance fee is approximately $18–25 USD and includes snorkel gear rental. Biodegradable sunscreen is mandatory — regular sunscreen is prohibited to protect the cenote ecosystem. Life jackets are available for non-swimmers. Book a tour or shuttle the day before to secure a spot.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely morning at Cancun Beach Resort. Take one last swim in the Caribbean, enjoy breakfast at a relaxed pace, and soak in the views. Pack souvenirs and gifts purchased throughout the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, visit Mercado 28 Street Food Tour for a final immersion in local Yucatecan culture and cuisine. Sample cochinita pibil, marquesitas (crispy rolled crepes), fresh juices, and browse artisan crafts for last-minute souvenirs. Mercado 28 is located in downtown Cancun (~20 min from Hotel Zone by taxi).
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport for departure. Allow at least 2–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security at Cancun International Airport.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — splurge on the full buffet if available, or enjoy eggs and fresh tropical fruit with coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mercado 28 — try a full spread of local dishes including panuchos, salbutes, and fresh agua de jamaica (hibiscus water). Budget ~$8–15 per person for a generous local meal.
meals.dinner: Light meal or snack at the airport before departure, or grab a final taco at a casual spot near the hotel before heading to the airport.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if your flight is in the evening. Mercado 28 is a great spot for affordable, authentic food and souvenir shopping — bargaining is acceptable at the craft stalls. Keep some pesos on hand for the market. Confirm airport transfer or taxi in advance.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Cancun International Airport at 11:00 AM on Flight AA. Private luxury transfer arranged to Cancun Beach Resort. Check-in, unpack, and settle into your premium suite with ocean views.
day_by_day.afternoon: After a light freshening up, head down to the resort's private beach for your first taste of the Caribbean. Enjoy a welcome cocktail poolside, take a leisurely swim, and soak in the turquoise waters. Arrange a beachside cabana for ultimate relaxation.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's rooftop or beachfront bar. Enjoy a welcome dinner at the resort's signature fine dining restaurant to ease into the trip without the need to travel.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport before boarding.
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at the resort's premium beach club — try fresh ceviche, grilled shrimp tacos, and tropical fruit platters paired with a chilled Michelada.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — indulge in a tasting menu featuring Yucatecan-inspired dishes such as lobster with achiote butter and chocolate lava cake with cajeta caramel.

day_by_day.notes: Flight lands at 11:00 AM — no morning activities scheduled. Pre-arrange a private airport transfer with the resort for a seamless arrival experience. Request early check-in in advance if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a gourmet breakfast at the resort before heading out for a full-day Isla Mujeres Snorkeling & Beach Tour. Depart via private ferry or luxury catamaran charter from Puerto Juárez or the Hotel Zone pier. Explore the crystal-clear Caribbean waters with a professional guided snorkeling session over vibrant coral reefs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive on Isla Mujeres and spend the afternoon exploring the charming town by golf cart. Visit Playa Norte, consistently ranked among the world's best beaches, and relax on its calm, shallow turquoise waters. Browse boutique shops along the main strip.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun via ferry as the sun sets over the Caribbean. Freshen up at the resort before heading out for dinner at a premium restaurant in the Hotel Zone.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the resort — eggs benedict, fresh tropical fruits, artisan pastries, and fresh-squeezed juices.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a top-rated seafood restaurant on Isla Mujeres such as Mango Café or Olivia Restaurant — try the grilled whole fish, lobster bisque, or Mediterranean-style seafood plates.
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Habichuela Sunset in Cancun's Hotel Zone — a legendary fine dining institution known for its cocobichuela (lobster and shrimp in tropical curry sauce served in a coconut) and romantic garden setting.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Isla Mujeres snorkeling tour in advance through a luxury operator for a private or small-group experience. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a light cover-up, and waterproof sandals. Ferry ride is approximately 20–30 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Full day at Playa Delfines Beach. Depart from the resort mid-morning by private car or taxi along the Hotel Zone boulevard (Blvd. Kukulcán). Arrive at one of Cancun's most scenic and uncrowded public beaches, famous for its panoramic views and the iconic Cancun sign. Set up a luxury beach setup — bring a cooler, premium beach towels, and a bluetooth speaker for a private beach day feel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue relaxing at Playa Delfines or take a short drive to explore the nearby El Rey Archaeological Zone, a smaller Mayan ruin site set right in the Hotel Zone — a unique and underrated experience with far fewer crowds than Tulum. Return to the beach for a final swim as the afternoon light turns golden.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a sunset spa treatment — book a couples' or solo massage, hydrotherapy session, or a traditional Mayan-inspired ritual at the resort spa. End the night with a romantic beachfront dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort's ocean-view terrace — avocado toast, smoked salmon, and a fresh açaí bowl.
meals.lunch: Pack a premium picnic lunch prepared by the resort, or dine at a nearby beach club such as Mandala Beach Club — enjoy gourmet bites, fresh cocktails, and VIP loungers.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Harry's Prime Steakhouse & Raw Bar in the Hotel Zone — renowned for its USDA Prime dry-aged steaks, premium sushi, and stunning lagoon views.

day_by_day.notes: Playa Delfines is a public beach with no entry fee and has excellent waves — ideal for bodyboarding. Parking is available but a private driver is recommended. The El Rey ruins are a hidden gem and typically very quiet — perfect for a quick 45-minute exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Tulum Ruins & Beach Combo Day Trip. Depart early by private luxury van (~2-hour drive south along the Riviera Maya). Arrive at the Tulum Archaeological Zone before the crowds for a private guided tour of the stunning Mayan ruins perched dramatically on seaside cliffs overlooking the Caribbean Sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from the ruins to the breathtaking beach below the cliffs for a swim in the turquoise waters. Afterward, explore Tulum town's bohemian beach strip — visit the iconic beach clubs such as Papaya Playa Project or Azulik for an afternoon cocktail and upscale ambiance in a stunning natural setting.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Cancun in the private van, arriving in the early evening. Freshen up at the resort and enjoy a relaxed evening with cocktails at a rooftop bar before a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure — granola, fruit, yogurt, and coffee to go.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Hartwood in Tulum — one of Mexico's most celebrated farm-to-table restaurants, featuring open-fire cooking with locally sourced ingredients. Reservations essential.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Porfirio's Cancun in the Hotel Zone — a sophisticated Mexican restaurant with an electric atmosphere, exceptional guacamole tableside, prime seafood, and premium tequila selection.

day_by_day.notes: Book a private guided tour of Tulum Ruins for the best experience — guides provide rich historical context about the Mayan civilization. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring sunscreen. Hartwood requires advance reservations — book at least a week ahead. Departure from hotel by 7:30 AM recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Cenote Dos Ojos Swimming & Snorkeling adventure. Depart by private luxury transfer (~1.5 hours south near Tulum). Arrive at the Dos Ojos cenote system — one of the world's longest underwater cave systems. Enjoy a private guided snorkeling or introductory cave diving experience through the magical crystal-clear freshwater caverns, stalactites, and halocline layers where fresh and salt water meet.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return north and stop at a premium beach club along the Riviera Maya coastline — consider Mamitas Beach Club in Playa del Carmen or a luxury resort day pass for an indulgent afternoon on the beach with VIP service, swimming, and relaxation before the final full evening in Cancun.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cancun for a special farewell-eve celebration. Enjoy a premium sunset cocktail cruise along the Hotel Zone lagoon or coastline, then close the night with Cancun's finest dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the resort — full American or Mexican breakfast spread with huevos rancheros, chilaquiles, fresh juices, and café de olla.
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at the premium beach club — fresh seafood platters, ceviche, and tropical cocktails.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tempo by Daniel Boulud at the Paradisus Cancun — a Michelin-starred chef's outpost offering French-Mediterranean cuisine with Caribbean influences in an elegant setting.

day_by_day.notes: Dos Ojos requires a short walk through jungle terrain — wear water shoes and bring a dry bag for your belongings. Life jackets and snorkeling gear are provided. Book a private guide for the cenote for an exclusive experience. The cocktail sunset cruise can be arranged through the resort's concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a slow, luxurious start. Take one last swim in the Caribbean Sea from the resort's private beach at sunrise or early morning when the light is golden and the beach is tranquil. Treat yourself to a final spa session or a yoga class on the beach if offered by the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: After checkout, if time permits before departure, visit Mercado 28 Street Food Tour for a cultural and culinary farewell to Cancun. Wander through the vibrant market, sample cochinita pibil, marquesitas (crispy crepes with Edam cheese and sweet fillings), freshly made tortillas, and tropical aguas frescas. Pick up artisan souvenirs, local crafts, and Mexican spices to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to Cancun International Airport for departure. Depart with unforgettable memories of the Caribbean.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet breakfast at the resort — order the full spread one last time. Treat yourself to freshly made pan dulce, tropical fruit, eggs to order, and a premium coffee or mimosa.
meals.lunch: Street food lunch at Mercado 28 — an authentic and flavorful farewell meal featuring Yucatecan classics at one of Cancun's most beloved local markets.
meals.dinner: Airport or departure meal — consider dining at one of the Cancun airport's premium lounges or grab a final taste of Mexico before boarding.

day_by_day.notes: Request a late checkout from the resort to maximize your final morning. Mercado 28 is located in downtown Cancun (not the Hotel Zone) — approximately 20 minutes by private car. Allow at least 2–3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. Confirm your private transfer to the airport through the resort concierge the evening before.
